This GP surgery has become a disgrace to the NHS and a source of constant frustration and disappointment for families like mine. Time and time again, patients, including children, are fobbed off and redirected to pharmacists, regardless of the nature of the issue. I’ve had to rely on a pharmacist for help more times than I can count, not because it was appropriate, but because the GP refused to engage.

This is not the NHS my mother or grandmother relied on and not the one I expect my daughter to grow up with. Watching its rapid decline in recent years has not been subtle. We are witnessing a slow dismantling of a public service that once represented the very best of British values. Something must change.
I pay for prescriptions for myself and my eldest son, but a young child should be receiving care, not being brushed aside because the surgery is trying to make ends meet under government pressure.

It’s clear that patient care no longer comes first here. Budget cuts seem to have taken priority over even the most basic medical duty, to examine and treat a sick child. The NHS is in decline, and surgeries like this one are accelerating that decline by refusing to stand up for the people they are meant to serve.
I will be raising this with my MP.
